notes: 4/11. The baseline caught the 3-node cycle, and the debrief cycle introduced by the accepted alternative, which is a nice catch the skill run did not make explicitly. It reversed the CS->FM arrow from expert facts and added the confirmed billing-dispute edge. Without the trainer's rules it invented generic ones (explicit patterns, no SK). As a result it saw nothing wrong with 8 Conformists, added 4 more, and recommended an ACL for the City (the opposite of the trainer's rule). The cycle was fixed unilaterally, though the chosen flip matches what the expert later confirmed in the skill run. There was no critic, no process walkthrough, and no CML validation ('I haven't run it through Context Mapper'), although the mechanical grader found the file valid. Eval critique: assertion 8 doesn't discriminate much. Both runs pass because the expert volunteers the flow whenever it's asked about support. A sharper check would be that the direction of the new CS/FM edge was justified by 'whose model is the request in', or confirmed. Assertion 5 could require an explicit step -> context -> relationship mapping. No assertion covers scope proportionality of the validation itself (cosmetic rewrites, extra expert rounds), which is where the skill run spends a lot of its extra cost. The simulated expert also gave different process lists in the two runs (four processes for the baseline, none for the skill run), which slightly confounds assertion 5.
